column1: # selftest-suite-timings.tsv — one row per suite whose measured cost feeds two independent
# which independently drifted while recording the SAME measurement for overlapping suites at
# different dates — e.g. lean-gate-selftest.sh was 141s in both, by coincidence, not by any
# reconciling mechanism). One row per suite now, one date.
# EACH CONSUMER APPLIES ITS OWN THRESHOLD, moved out of this file and into the consumer that
# reads it (#641): tools/run-selftests.sh and tools/check-sweep-bound.sh at 9s (the directive
# below), tools/mutation-sweep.sh at 5s (a separate, hardcoded consumer-side constant, unchanged
# by this file). A suite between the two — at or above 5s but under 9s — is a real row here,
# relevant to the mutation lane only; run-selftests.sh filters it out at read time.
# tools/check-sweep-bound.sh's aggregate ratchet (#629) also lives in this file now, replacing
# tools/selftest-sweep-baseline.tsv — the two directive lines below. Still an EXPLICIT REVIEWED
# COMMIT to re-baseline, never an automatic rewrite; only the file it lives in changed.
# A row naming no discovered suite is a HARD ERROR (run-selftests.sh's existing stale-row
# posture, applied here too). A suite ABSENT from this file is treated as fast by both consumers.
